title: Shared definitions
description:
Values that more than one schema needs, in one place.

Codex, chunk 0 round 6: these lived inside incident.schema.json and were referenced from the other files by absolute id. Every ref resolved in production, because the validator registers all schemas together — but it made two formerly independent files silently depend on the incident schema, and an absolute $ref is only a name: nothing fetches the file it points at.

The schemas are a package, not four separate documents. Nothing here compiles alone, and a test checks that every cross-file reference points at a schema the validator actually registers.

evidenceSource.description: Where a fact came from. One carrier: this list also governs what a chat answer may cite, and the two drifting apart would let a message cite a source no evidence can have. `root_cause` was added on 2026-09-07: the verdict's evidence is traced back to the agent that reported the citation, and when no agent did — which the citation rule makes unreachable in practice, and this does not rely on that — the claim is laid at the root cause agent's own door rather than at a provider's. `datadog` names the alerting source; it is the one value no observation slot can produce, so attributing a slot's fact to it was the definition of inventing one.

severity.description: One carrier for how bad something is, shared by an incoming alert and by an agent's finding.

causeCode.description: The named causes this system can identify. One carrier, referenced by both the incident's root_cause_code and an agent's hypothesis code. Codex, 2026-09-05: keeping them as two enums that a test compares means the lists can still be written apart and only caught afterwards - and one such drift had already made a scenario unsolvable, with CPU_THROTTLING recordable while no agent could propose it. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is deliberately NOT here: it is a verdict about a whole incident, not a cause an agent can hold a hypothesis about.

provenance.description:
Where an observation came from, carried by the observation itself.

Codex, 2026-09-05, naming the question no content check can answer: 'Does this observation come from the trusted collection request that created this incident? Content scanning cannot establish provenance. A foreign record may contain no incident ID, while a legitimate log may mention another ID.'

Everything before this trusted an observation because it looked right. This is the only thing that can say it was asked for, for this incident, from this cluster, in one collection.

collection_id.description: The one request that gathered this. Every slot of one incident must carry the same value: three observations from three separate collections do not describe one moment, and agents read them as though they do.

requested_for.description: Which incident it was gathered for. An observation asked for elsewhere is not this incident's, however well it fits.

cluster.description: Which cluster it came from. Data from another cluster looks entirely ordinary, which is why nothing downstream can catch it.

provider.description: Which implementation produced it. Recorded so a defect can be traced to a provider rather than to the agents reading it.
